extracted.intended_audience: conference program committee chairs, PC members, conference organizers, and researchers involved in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for improving the quality and fairness of conference peer review in computer science, focusing on review process design (double-blind reviewing, external review committees), author response, and program committee practices (in-person meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified expert reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewing seeks to evaluate research using qualified experts, who have the scientific training, experience, and skills to judge the merit of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reviewers with appropriate scientific training, experience, and domain skills; prioritize reviewer expertise as a primary quality requirement for producing reliable assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind until accept
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) double-blind until accept to further reduce bias and enable rejected submission to remain blind in subsequent submissions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain author anonymity through the decision and only reveal identities after acceptance so as to reduce nepotism and bias and so rejected papers can remain blind on resubmission; note that implementation practices vary across venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: External review committees (vs ad hoc assignments)
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) the need for external review committees (versus ad hoc assignments) to handle increasing numbers and breadth of submissions, ease the implementation of double-blind reviewing, and improve overall review quality with more expert reviews
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standing or external committees to increase reviewer expertise coverage, scale to growing submission volumes, make double-blind assignment easier, and improve consistency and overall review quality compared to ad hoc reviewer assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response to improve reviewer accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) the use of author response to improve reviewer accountability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide authors a structured opportunity to respond to reviews to correct misunderstandings, provide clarifications, and prompt reviewers to reconsider or refine assessments, increasing accountability and potentially improving final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person program committee meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) in person program committee meetings to communicate, establish, and constantly apply scientific standards and build community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold face-to-face PC meetings to enable discussion, align and apply scientific standards consistently, and build community and shared norms; seen as a mechanism for improving reviewing accountability ('trust and verify'). The author views this as undervalued relative to other interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review should address core challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Current challenges for peer reviewing in computer science include (1) obtaining expert reviews as the breadth and depth of our field grows; (2) accommodating growth in the amount of research, number of researchers, and submissions; and (3) incorporating best practices based on social science research on nepotism and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design review processes and practices (e.g., reviewer selection, committee structure, anonymity policies, and response mechanisms) specifically to: secure sufficient domain expertise; scale to increased submission volume and field breadth; and mitigate nepotism and bias using evidence-based practices.
